title: Substring With Largest Variance
summary: The variance of a string is the greatest difference in the frequency of any two characters within the string.
statement: The variance of a string is the greatest difference in the frequency of any two characters within the string. Given a string s made of lowercase English letters, find the maximum variance among all its substrings.
constraints: For a substring and two distinct characters both present in it, variance is frequency(major)-frequency(minor).
Choose any ordered character pair and any nonempty contiguous substring.
Return the maximum variance, or zero when s has fewer than two distinct characters.
hints: Fix an ordered pair of major and minor characters and scan like a constrained Kadane algorithm.
Track their count difference, update only after seeing a minor, and reset a negative segment only when another minor remains.
Repeat for every ordered distinct pair and keep the greatest major_count-minor_count.
Every optimal substring has some ordered frequency pair; the reset discards only prefixes that cannot improve a future valid segment.
editorial: Every optimal substring has some ordered frequency pair; the reset discards only prefixes that cannot improve a future valid segment.

tests.explanation: In substring babbb, b occurs four times and a once, giving variance three.
Every substring containing two characters has equal one-one counts, so the maximum is zero.
